'''Gian Francesco Giudice''' (born 25 January 1961) is an Italian [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] specializing in [[particle physics]] and [[cosmology]]. He has spent most of his career at [[CERN]], where he served as the Head of the Theoretical Physics Department for ten years. His research primarily focuses on developing new theories that expand our current understanding of the particle world and on exploring how these theories can describe the early stages of the universe's history.

== Academic career ==
After graduating in [[physics]] from the [[University of Padua]] in 1984, Giudice earned his PhD in [[theoretical physics]] from the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in [[Trieste]] in 1988. He worked as a Research Associate at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] near [[Chicago]] from 1988 to 1990. He then became a Research Fellow in the Physics Department of the [[University of Texas]] at [[Austin, Texas|Austin]], in the group led by [[Steven Weinberg]]. After being employed by the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] of [[Italy]], in 1993 he moved to [[CERN]], where he served as the Head of the [[Theoretical Physics]] Department from 2016 to 2025. He has then become a Professor of Physics at [[New York University Abu Dhabi]]. Giudice has been elected academician of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]], the [[Istituto Veneto di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti]], [[Accademia Galileiana]] and the [[World Academy of Art and Science]]. His accolades include the Jacques Solvay Chair in Physics at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] (2013), Distinguished Visiting Research Chair at [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] (2019), Sackler Distinguished Lecturer at [[Tel Aviv University]] (2020), Chandrasekhar Lecturer at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (2022) and Erwin-Schrödinger Professor at the [[University of Vienna]] (2023).

== Research ==
Giudice's research activity mainly deals with theories of fundamental forces that extend beyond the [[Standard Model]], as well the role of [[supersymmetry]] and [[Dimension (mathematics and physics)|extra dimensions]] in the microscopic realm. He is also studying how these theories can be applied to [[cosmology]] in order to explain the early evolution of the [[universe]]. His most notable results are in the areas of [[supersymmetry]], [[Dimension (mathematics and physics)|extra dimensions]], [[Electroweak interaction|electroweak physics]], [[collider]] physics, [[dark matter]], and [[Leptogenesis (physics)|leptogenesis]]. Together with physicist [[Riccardo Barbieri]], he proposed<ref>{{cite journal|author1=R. Barbieri |author2=G. F. Giudice |title= Upper Bounds on Supersymmetric Particle Masses|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 306|issue=1 |pages=63–76|year= 1988|doi= 10.1016/0550-3213(88)90171-X|bibcode = 1988NuPhB.306...63B |url= https://cds.cern.ch/record/180560/files/198711060.pdf}}</ref> a widely used criterion for evaluating the degree of naturalness of [[supersymmetry|supersymmetric theories]] that achieve [[electroweak symmetry breaking]]. He co-invented the [[Mu problem|Giudice-Masiero mechanism]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=A. Masiero |title= A Natural Solution to the Mu Problem in Supergravity Theories|journal=Phys. Lett. B|volume= 206|issue=3 |pages=480–484|year= 1988|doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(88)91613-9|bibcode = 1988PhLB..206..480G }}</ref> which is the leading explanation for the [[mu problem]] of [[supergravity]]. He has made fundamental contributions to the construction of [[Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model|Gauge Mediation]],<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=R. Rattazzi |title= Theories with gauge mediated supersymmetry breaking |journal=Phys. Rep.|volume= 322|issue=6 |pages=419–499|year= 1999|doi= 10.1016/S0370-1573(99)00042-3|arxiv = hep-ph/9801271|bibcode = 1999PhR...322..419G |s2cid=118928206 }}</ref> and he co-proposed [[Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model|Anomaly Mediation]]<ref>{{cite journal|author1=L. Randall |author2=R. Sundrum |title= Out of this world supersymmetry breaking |journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 557|issue=1–2 |pages=79–118|year= 1999|doi= 10.1016/S0550-3213(99)00359-4|arxiv = hep-th/9810155|bibcode = 1999NuPhB.557...79R |s2cid=1408101 }}{{br}}{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=M. A. Luty |author3=H. Murayama |author4=R. Rattazzi |title= Gaugino mass without singlets |journal=JHEP|volume= 9812|issue=12 |page=027|year= 1998|doi= 10.1088/1126-6708/1998/12/027|arxiv = hep-ph/9810442|bibcode = 1998JHEP...12..027G |s2cid=12517291 }}</ref> and [[Split supersymmetry|Split Supersymmetry]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=N. Arkani-Hamed |author2=S. Dimopoulos |title= Supersymmetric unification without low energy supersymmetry and signatures for fine-tuning at the LHC|journal=JHEP|volume= 0506|issue=6 |page=073|year= 2006|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2005/06/073|arxiv = hep-th/0405159|bibcode = 2005JHEP...06..073A |s2cid=6658196 }}{{br}}{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=A. Romanino |title= Split supersymmetry|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 699|issue=1 |page=65|year= 2004|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2004.11.048|arxiv = hep-ph/0406088|bibcode = 2005NuPhB.706..487G }}{{br}}{{cite journal|author1=N. Arkani-Hamed |author2=S. Dimopoulos |author3=G. F. Giudice |author4=A. Romanino |title= Aspects of split supersymmetry|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 709|issue=1–2 |pages=3–46|year= 2005|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2004.12.026|arxiv = hep-ph/0409232|bibcode = 2005NuPhB.709....3A |s2cid=16632949 }}</ref> He is one of the proponents of a method<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=R. Rattazzi |title= Extracting supersymmetry breaking effects from wave function renormalization |journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 511|issue=1–2 |pages=25–44|year= 1998|doi= 10.1016/S0550-3213(97)00647-0|arxiv = hep-ph/9706540|bibcode = 1998NuPhB.511...25G |s2cid=5764178 }}{{br}}{{cite journal|author1=N. Arkani-Hamed |author2=G. F. Giudice |author3=M. A. Luty |author4=R. Rattazzi |title= Supersymmetry breaking loops from analytic continuation into superspace|journal=Phys. Rev. D|volume= 58|issue=11 |article-number=115005|year= 1998|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevD.58.115005|arxiv = hep-ph/9803290|bibcode = 1998PhRvD..58k5005A |s2cid=13376937 }}</ref> to compute [[Quantum mechanics|quantum effects]] in theories with broken [[supersymmetry]] through [[analytic continuation]] into [[superspace]]. His approach<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. F. Giudice |author2=R. Rattazzi |author3=J. D. Wells |title= Quantum gravity and extra dimensions at high-energy colliders|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 544|issue=1–2 |pages=3–38|year= 1999|doi= 10.1016/S0550-3213(99)00044-9|arxiv = hep-ph/9811291|bibcode = 1999NuPhB.544....3G |s2cid=14407490 }}</ref> to describing [[graviton]] interactions in theories with [[large extra dimensions|extra spatial dimensions]] is largely utilized for studies at the [[Large Hadron Collider]]. He is also one of the originators of the idea of Minimal Flavor Violation,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. D'Ambrosio |author2=G. F. Giudice |author3=G. Isidori |author4=A. Strumia |title= Minimal flavor violation: an effective field theory approach|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 645|issue=1–2 |pages=155–187|year= 2002|doi= 10.1016/S0550-3213(02)00836-2|arxiv = hep-ph/9811291|bibcode = 2002NuPhB.645..155D |s2cid=2049412 }}</ref> a paradigm to characterize the effects of [[flavor (particle physics)|flavor]] transitions in new theories of [[particle physics]]. After the discovery of the [[Higgs Boson|Higgs boson]], he computed the probability that the Higgs vacuum undergoes [[quantum tunneling]], finding the surprising result that the [[universe]] is in a critical state, which will eventually end in a cosmic collapse.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=G. Degrassi |author2=S. Di Vita |author3=J. Elias-Miro |author4=J. R. Espinosa |author5=G. F. Giudice |author6=G. Isidori |author7=A. Strumia |title= Higgs mass and vacuum stability in the Standard Model at NNLO|journal=JHEP|volume= 1208|issue=8 |page=098|year= 2012|doi= 10.1007/JHEP08(2012)098|arxiv = 1205.6497|bibcode = 2012JHEP...08..098D |s2cid=53368704 }}</ref>

== Support of particle accelerator projects ==
Giudice has been actively involved in studying the physics potential of [[particle accelerators]], advocating and supporting several new projects at [[CERN]] and in other laboratories around the world. He has been a member of the ''LHC Experiments Committee'' (the body that reviews the activity of the experimental groups at the [[LHC]]), the ''European Committee for Future Accelerators'' (the advisory body for long-range planning of high-energy facilities in [[Europe]]), the preparatory group for the 2020 [[European Strategy for Particle Physics]], and numerous advisory and review committees of research institutes worldwide.

== Science popularization ==
Besides his research work, Giudice is active in outreach efforts. He frequently gives public lectures on [[particle physics]] and related topics, and participates in science festivals and other events. He is the author of ''[https://web.archive.org/web/20131101054656/http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-eng.html A Zeptospace Odyssey]'',<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-eng.html A Zeptospace Odyssey: A Journey into the Physics of the LHC] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101054656/http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-eng.html |date=2013-11-01 }}'', Oxford University Press, Oxford 2010, {{ISBN|978-0-19-958191-7}}.</ref> a popular science book on the physics of the [[LHC]], which has been finalist for the [http://padovacultura.padovanet.it/homepage-6.0/2012/05/premio_letterario_galileo_2012_1.html 2012 Galileo Literary Prize] and the Prize Pianeta Galileo 2013. Originally written in English, the book has been translated into Italian,<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-ita.html Odissea nello zeptospazio: un viaggio nella fisica dell'LHC]'', Springer-Verlag Italia, Milano 2010, {{ISBN|978-88-470-1630-9}}.</ref> German,<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-ger.html Odyssee im Zeptoraum: Eine Reise in die Physik des LHC]'', Springer-Verlag, Berlin Heidelberg 2012, {{ISBN|978-3-642-22394-5}}.</ref> French,<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-fra.html L'Odyssée du Zeptoespace: Un voyage au cœur de la physique du LHC]'', [[Presses polytechniques et universitaires romandes]], Lausanne 2013, {{ISBN|978-2-88-074998-9}}.</ref> Spanish,<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-spa.html Odisea en el zeptoespacio]'', Jot Down Books, Madrid 2013, {{ISBN|978-84-940939-1-3}}.</ref> and Korean.<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[http://giudice.web.cern.ch/giudice/zeptospace/zepto-kor.html 젭토스페이스 - 힉스 입자를 발견한 LHC 물리학의 세계]'', Humanist, Seoul 2017, {{ISBN|979-11-608-0004-3}}.</ref> Giudice is also the author of ''[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-69933-7 Before the Big Bang]''<ref>G. F. Giudice, ''[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-69933-7 Before the Big Bang]'', Copernicus Books Springer, Berlin 2024, {{ISBN|978-30-316-9932-0}}.</ref>, a popular science book that explores the origin of the universe. The book has been translated into six languages and has been finalist for the [https://www.triestenext.it/news/trieste-next-cinque-finalisti-per-il-libro-scientifico-dellanno/ Science Book of the Year Trieste Next 2024], [https://cosmos.cittametropolitana.rc.it Cosmos Prize 2024] and [https://www.premiodivulgazionescientifica.it/la-quindicina-del-premio-nazionale-di-divulgazione-scientifica-2024/ Premio Nazionale di Divulgazione Scientifica 2024 - Giancarlo Dosi].
